summary: This lecture tells about Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, the richest man in Mecca. The ustaz opens with the Prophet SAW reciting Surah An-Najm before the Kaaba, when everyone including the polytheists prostrated except Al-Walid, who only put soil on his forehead. The Prophet SAW hoped Al-Walid would embrace Islam because of his influence, but he was arrogant and refused to sit with the blind Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, so Surah Abasa was revealed. False news that all of Mecca had embraced Islam made some companions return from Abyssinia, but most went back again. Mus'ab ibn Umair, however, returned to Mecca, lost his wealth when his mother told him to leave, and lived simply. The ustaz also tells a little of Khalid ibn al-Walid, Al-Walid's son who would later embrace Islam, and of Najashi who hid his Islam.
keyPoints: The Prophet SAW recited Surah An-Najm and everyone prostrated except the arrogant Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah.
Al-Walid was the richest man, called Al-Wahid because he alone paid for the Kaaba's covering every year.
Surah Abasa was revealed when he frowned because the blind Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum interrupted his meeting with Al-Walid.
False news that all of Mecca had embraced Islam made some companions return from Abyssinia before going back.
Mus'ab returned to Mecca and lived poor after his mother drove him out without wealth.

chapters.title: Surah An-Najm and the prostration
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW recited Surah An-Najm before the Kaaba and everyone prostrated, except Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah who put soil on his forehead.

chapters.title: Lenggong and Prophet Adam
chapters.summary: The ustaz recalls the visit to Lenggong, home of Perak Man, and the story of Habil and Qabil who learned from a crow how to bury the dead.

chapters.title: Recap of Abyssinia and Mecca
chapters.summary: The ustaz recalls Najashi and Ja'far and says the Prophet SAW in Mecca looked for a great man to bring to Islam so that Islam would be strong.

chapters.title: The richest man in Mecca
chapters.summary: Al-Walid was called Al-Wahid because he alone paid for the new Kaaba covering each year, not sharing with Abu Jahal and Abu Sufyan.

chapters.title: The Prophet SAW approaches Al-Walid
chapters.summary: Al-Walid was powerful, rich and a poet, so he tried to convey Islam to him until Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum arrived.

chapters.title: Al-Walid's arrogance
chapters.summary: Al-Walid refused to sit with a blind, poor man. The Prophet frowned and Allah sent down Quran telling him to focus on those who want to learn.

chapters.title: False news from Mecca
chapters.summary: The Muslims in Abyssinia heard that all of Mecca had embraced Islam and rushed home.

chapters.title: The polytheists prostrate
chapters.summary: The recitation of Surah An-Najm was so beautiful that Quraysh also prostrated, except Al-Walid, and that was the source of the false news.

chapters.title: Leave him to Me
chapters.summary: Allah mentions in Surah Al-Muddaththir the one created alone, rich and arrogant. Abu Jahal incited him.

chapters.title: Looking for a label for the Prophet SAW
chapters.summary: Abu Jahal wanted to label him a liar or insane, but Al-Walid refused because they knew he never lied, until finally choosing sorcerer.

chapters.title: Returning from Abyssinia
chapters.summary: The companions returned happily but were told at the border that Meccans had not embraced Islam, so most went back, except Mus'ab.

chapters.title: Mus'ab's mother drives him out
chapters.summary: His mother offered wealth if he left the Prophet SAW, but he refused, and was driven out without wealth to live simply in tattered clothes.

chapters.title: Abu Jahal's campaign and Abu Bakr beaten
chapters.summary: Abu Jahal followed him telling people not to listen, but more embraced Islam, and Abu Bakr was beaten until bruised.

chapters.title: Appreciating ease, and Abyssinia
chapters.summary: The early generation valued the shahada, and the companions in Abyssinia supported the just Najashi until he died and was prayed for in absentia.

chapters.title: Khalid ibn al-Walid
chapters.summary: The ustaz mentions Khalid, trained in riding and archery, a great commander who would embrace Islam, and the event of Hudaybiyyah.

chapters.title: Recap and Al-Walid's death
chapters.summary: Al-Walid did not embrace Islam and died before the Battle of Badr when his foot was wounded by something sharp.

events.title: Seeking a label for the Prophet SAW
events.desc: Al-Walid rejected liar and insane and chose sorcery.

events.label: Return
events.title: Companions return from Abyssinia
events.desc: False news made them return, and most went back.

events.label: Mus'ab
events.title: Mus'ab is driven out by his mother

lessons.title: Arrogance blocks guidance
lessons.body: Al-Walid was spellbound by the Quran but arrogant and refused to prostrate.

lessons.title: Honour those who sincerely learn
lessons.body: Allah told him to focus on the blind man who truly wanted to learn.

lessons.title: Baseless accusations
lessons.body: The Prophet's own enemies admitted he was neither a liar nor insane.

lessons.title: Prohibition raises interest
lessons.body: The more Abu Jahal forbade, the more people listened to the Prophet SAW.

lessons.title: Faith above wealth
lessons.body: Mus'ab refused his mother's wealth rather than leave the Prophet SAW.

lessons.title: Appreciating the ease of believing
lessons.body: The earliest generation deeply valued the shahada because it was hard to utter.

lessons.title: Be careful with news
lessons.body: The news that all of Mecca was Muslim was untrue and caused hardship.

lessons.title: The Prophet SAW skilfully avoids conflict
lessons.body: At Hudaybiyyah he took another road to avoid clashing with Khalid.
